title: hosted-api-marginal-cost-fingerprinting-by-session-type
summary: Working spreadsheet + narrative that breaks hosted API unit economics into micro-marginal components by session type (one-shot completion, multi-turn chat, streaming, embeddings). Goal is to expose which session patterns drive non-linear COGS and where caching/routing/slotting levers yield the largest per-token/marginal savings.
methodology: We move beyond per-token averages and compute a marginal cost fingerprint: 1) classify sessions into discrete types by request shape and cacheability; 2) bucket by request percentiles (p50/p75/p90/p99) for input length and output length; 3) attribute GPU-time, amortized license, network, KMS, and infra overhead to each bucket using observed telemetry; 4) simulate cache hit rates & batching sensitivity to estimate delta PPK for each lever. Assumptions and formulas are inline in the sheet cells.
inputs:
Primary inputs (sheet tabs):
- telemetry_session_samples.csv: sample of 100k requests (fields: session_id, session_type, user_prompt_tokens, response_tokens, streaming_flag, region, timestamp)
- infra_costs tab: GPU hourly price by region, license amortization per-GPU-hour, average slot-utilization by time-slice
- network_and_storage tab: per-request egress and request-count ops estimates
- model_profiles tab: per-model latency per-token, kv-cache hit effectiveness by prefix-length
- business_assumptions tab: customer pricing, margin targets, SLA tiers.
All inputs base month = Dec 2024; costs normalized to USD/month. Date ranges: 2024-10 to 2024-12 aggregated for seasonality smoothing.
scenarios:
We run three lever scenarios across the fingerprint:
- Baseline (current telemetry)
- Cache-opt (increase prefix cache hit by +15pp via prefix index and TTL tuning)
- Slot-tilt (rebalance slot types to favor low-latency one-shot buckets during peak; reduces amortized idling)
For each scenario the sheet projects marginal PPK (USD per 1k tokens) by session_type and overall blended PPK. Also includes region splits for us-east/us-west/eu-central with spot vs reserve blends.
key_findings:
1) Multi-turn long chats (22% of traffic) are ~2.8x the blended marginal PPK because they dominate single-request KV cache misses and force longer kv cache lifetimes.
2) Streaming workloads have high output token counts but low cacheability — however they are sensitive to batching and can see 20-35% PPK reduction under continuous-batching improvements.
3) One-shot completions are low per-session latency but represent largest volume; small cache wins (even +10pp) yield outsized savings on blended dollar costs.
4) Region mix matters: EU region GPU price + network egress increases PPK by ~18% vs us-east for identical session shapes.
5) Slot-tilt reduces amortized license per-token by 9% in peak windows but increases tail latency slightly; recommend coupling with SLA-aware route policies.
recommendations:
Short-term (30-60 days):
- Implement targeted prefix-cache pilot for high-volume one-shot endpoints (top 10 routes) and track cache-hit per route.
- Add a session-type label to production telemetry to make fingerprinting first-class in the data pipeline.
- Run a 2-week slot-tilt experiment in us-east on non-SLA trials to validate license amortization numbers.
Medium-term (90 days):
- Roll out continuous-batching improvements for streaming routes with adaptive batch windows.
- Introduce region-specific price-to-route policies that route non-sensitive low-latency requests to lower-cost zones.
Long-term:
- Productize a per-route econ simulator in the Console that shows expected PPK under configurable cache/hit/slot assumptions for customers.

notes_and_uncertainties:
- Cacheability estimates are sensitive to prompt engineering and customer behavior shifts; pilot results may diverge.
- Telemetry sampling bias: telemetry_session_samples.csv excludes some very large enterprise sessions due to PII filters; this could understate long-chat costs.
- Model family differences: quantized vs fp16 variants have different per-token compute curves; sheet currently normalizes to a weighted-average profile and flags model-specific deltas in a separate tab.
- Networking/edge egress assumptions are placeholder and need validation with infra billing exports.
- This doc intentionally focuses on marginal deltas; absolute COGS reconciliation to finance will be a follow-up (linked JIRA).
